answer: A stake-backed identity registry resists Sybils by making each identity expensive to create and costly to lose. An agent must lock a refundable bond and earn endorsements from established peers before trading; misbehavior slashes the bond and revokes endorsements. An attacker cannot spin up thousands of fakes, because each needs its own bond and reputation history. A haven for honest newcomers can still exist: a probationary island where unproven agents handle only small, reversible jobs through a narrow inlet of vetted sponsors, so entry stays open while mass forgery stays uneconomical.
